title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the combinatorics of the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, meaning the boundary strata of the stable compactification. The previous page treats an algebraically closed field k. There a 'standard curve' X (a nodal curve with punctures) is shown to be equivalent, for isomorphisms, to the data (Y, Ã, I, σ):
- Y is the normalization of the completion X̂.
- Ã ⊂ Y(k) is the set of preimages of the nodes.
- I is the set of punctures.
- σ is the fixed-point-free involution of Ã that pairs the two branches at each node.

This page extends the definition to an arbitrary base S. A standard curve over S is defined 'constructively' from a system (5):
- (a) Y → S is proper and smooth, of relative dimension 1 everywhere.
- (b) Ã and I are closed subschemes of Y, finite étale over S, with Ã ∩ I = ∅.
- (c) σ_Ã is an involution of Ã acting freely.

One forms the pinching X̂ = Y/σ. This is the pushout of Y ← Ã → A = Ã/σ, a nodal curve over S whose nodes are not smoothed: it is an equisingular, 'clutched' family. X̂ contains A and I as closed subschemes finite étale over S, and one sets X = X̂ \ I.

Claim (6): the functor (Y, Ã, I, σ) ↦ X, from systems (5) with isomorphisms to relative S-schemes with isomorphisms, is fully faithful. Grothendieck then writes 'faux tel quel!' and a marginal NB that the functor must be corrected. The next page's margin gives the fix: either take S reduced, or, better, replace X by the pair (X̂, I), so that X = X̂ − I. The problem only arises when I ≠ ∅.

The defect is real. Take S = Spec k[ε], Y = P^1, I = {∞}, so X = A^1_S. Then x ↦ x + εx^3 is an S-automorphism of A^1_S. In the coordinate t = 1/x it becomes t ↦ t − ε/t, so it does not extend to P^1_S. Isomorphisms of punctured curves over non-reduced bases need not extend across the punctures, so full faithfulness fails.

When I = ∅ the statement is fine. Isomorphisms preserve the singular locus (Fitting ideal of Ω), and Y can be recovered by blowing up that locus, compatibly with base change for these equisingular families. With pairs (X̂, I), full faithfulness holds over any S.

Purpose: this gives a functorial description of the boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}. Such a stratum is the quotient of a product of smaller moduli spaces by the automorphisms of a dual graph, which is built on the next page from π_0(Y), Ã, A and I.
errors: Claim (6), as stated for an arbitrary base S, is false when I ≠ ∅. Over non-reduced S, automorphisms of X = X̂ − I need not extend to X̂. Example: x ↦ x + εx^3 on A^1 over k[ε]. Grothendieck flags this himself ('faux tel quel!'), and the next page corrects it by using the pair (X̂, I) or by restricting to reduced S.

Minor: the definition implicitly needs Ã and I closed in Y and the quotient to exist as a scheme. The pushout along a finite étale closed subscheme with a free involution does exist (Ferrand pinching), but this is not stated.

ideas.what: Nodal curve over S obtained by pinching a smooth proper curve along a finite étale subscheme with a free involution (equisingular nodal family).
ideas.modern_name: Clutching / gluing morphisms; pinching (pushout) of schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (clutching morphisms, 1983); Ferrand (pinching, 'Conducteur, descente et pincement', 2003)
ideas.where_published: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} are discussed informally in Esquisse d'un programme; not this construction explicitly

ideas.what: Equivalence between standard (pointed nodal) curves and normalization data (Y, Ã, I, σ), extended over a base; failure of full faithfulness over non-reduced bases for punctured curves, fixed by using (X̂, I).
ideas.modern_name: Description of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} via stable graphs and normalization; open curves versus compactified pointed curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; standard in the theory of stable curves

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard foundational setup: clutching and normalization data for nodal curves over a base. Grothendieck's self-correction, that punctured curves must be replaced by their compactifications with marked divisor over non-reduced bases, is well known. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'sera défini' should read 'sera définie' (it refers to 'une courbe standard').
In (6), the inserted '{+?+}' before I is a stray stroke or comma in the handwriting, not a question mark.
The insertion in the 'systèmes (5)' line reads '(pour les iso)'.
The bottom marginal note is very uncertain. It reads roughly 'NB NB cet foncteur est à corriger (6)... i.e. ...' and is followed on the main text by 'faux tel quel!'.
The page number at the lower left is 6.
